QuestionText: Metals are generally:
Options: B) Good conductors of heat and electricity
Explanation: Metals: good conductors (heat, electricity), lustrous, malleable, ductile, high density, high melting point. Non-metals: opposite properties generally.

QuestionText: The property of metals to be drawn into thin wires is called:
Explanation: Ductility: ability to be drawn into wires. Gold is most ductile. Malleability: ability to be beaten into thin sheets (gold most malleable).

QuestionText: The property of metals to be beaten into thin sheets is called:
Explanation: Malleability: hammered into thin sheets without breaking. Gold is most malleable. Used in gold foil, aluminium foil.

QuestionText: Sodium (Na) is stored in kerosene because:
Options: B) It is highly reactive with air and water
C) It needs to be kept cool
Explanation: Na is highly reactive: Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂ (heat). Catches fire spontaneously with air. Stored in kerosene (oil) to prevent contact with air and water.

QuestionText: The reactivity series (activity series) lists metals in order of:
Explanation: Reactivity series (top to bottom, decreasing): K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H, Cu, Ag, Au, Pt. More reactive metals displace less reactive from compounds.

QuestionText: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
Explanation: Silver has highest electrical conductivity, but copper is used commercially (cheaper). Gold doesn't tarnish but very expensive. Aluminium: lightweight conductor.

QuestionText: Mercury is unique among metals because it is:
Explanation: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal liquid at room temperature. Gallium melts at 29.8°C (just above room temperature). Mercury used in thermometers, barometers, switches.

QuestionText: When metals react with oxygen, they form:
Explanation: 4Na + O₂ → 2Na₂O. 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Metal + oxygen → metal oxide. Metal oxides are generally basic (react with acids).

QuestionText: Non-metals that exist as gases at room temperature include:
Explanation: Gaseous non-metals at room temp: H₂, O₂, N₂, F₂, Cl₂, noble gases. Liquid: Br₂. Solids: C, S, P, I₂, Se.

QuestionText: Ionic compounds have:
Options: B) Poor conductivity in solid state
C) Good conductivity when dissolved or molten
Explanation: Ionic compounds: high melting/boiling points, hard, conduct electricity in solution or molten state (ions free to move), poor conductors as solids (ions fixed).

QuestionText: Thermite reaction involves:
Explanation: Thermite: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. Al is more reactive than Fe, displaces Fe. Extremely exothermic (2500°C). Used to weld iron rails.

QuestionText: Alloys are made to:
Options: B) Improve strength, corrosion resistance, or other properties
Explanation: Alloys improve properties: stainless steel (corrosion resistant), brass (harder than Cu), bronze (strong), duralumin (lightweight, strong).

QuestionText: Copper does NOT react with dilute HCl because:
Options: B) Copper is below hydrogen in reactivity series (cannot displace H)
Explanation: Cu is below H in reactivity series → cannot displace H₂ from acid. Metals above H (Zn, Fe, Mg, Al) displace H₂ from dilute acids.

QuestionText: Galvanisation is coating iron with:
Explanation: Galvanisation: iron coated with zinc. Zinc is more reactive → acts as sacrificial anode → corrodes in place of iron. Protects even when coating is scratched.

QuestionText: The ore from which aluminium is extracted is:
Explanation: Bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O): main ore of aluminium. Haematite (Fe₂O₃): iron. Galena (PbS): lead. Chalcopyrite (CuFeS₂): copper.

QuestionText: Iron is extracted from haematite (Fe₂O₃) by:
Options: B) Chemical reduction by carbon (coke) in blast furnace
Explanation: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ in blast furnace. Carbon (coke) reduces iron oxide. High reactivity metals (Al, Mg, Na) extracted by electrolysis.

QuestionText: Non-metals on reacting with oxygen form:
Explanation: Non-metal oxides are acidic: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃. SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃. Dissolved in water → acids. Metal oxides are basic.

QuestionText: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of:
Explanation: Carbon allotropes: diamond (hardest natural substance, non-conductor), graphite (soft, lubricant, conductor), fullerene (C₆₀), graphene.

QuestionText: Graphite conducts electricity because:
Options: B) It has free electrons due to delocalised pi bonds
Explanation: Graphite: each C forms 3 bonds → 1 free electron per atom → delocalised electron cloud → conducts electricity. Diamond: 4 bonds per C → no free electrons → insulator.

QuestionText: The most abundant metal in Earth's crust is:
Explanation: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust (~8%). Iron is 2nd. Silicon is the most abundant non-metal (~28% of crust).

QuestionText: Noble metals like gold and platinum are unreactive because:
Options: B) They have very low ionisation energy
C) They are at the bottom of the reactivity series (very low reactivity)
Explanation: Noble metals (Au, Pt) are at bottom of reactivity series → extremely low reactivity → found as free metals in nature → used in jewellery.

QuestionText: Electrolysis of alumina (Al₂O₃) produces:
Options: A) Al at cathode, O₂ at anode
B) O₂ at cathode, Al at anode
Explanation: Hall-Héroult process: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al (at cathode). 2O²⁻ → O₂ + 4e⁻ (at anode). Molten Na₃AlF₆ (cryolite) lowers melting point of Al₂O₃.

QuestionText: Phosphorus is stored under water because:
Options: A) It is soluble in water
B) White phosphorus is highly reactive with oxygen
C) It needs water to stay active
Explanation: White phosphorus (P₄) ignites spontaneously in air. Stored under water to prevent contact with oxygen. Like Na stored in kerosene.

QuestionText: Metals react with water to produce:
Explanation: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂↑. Mg + H₂O (steam) → MgO + H₂. Metal + water → metal hydroxide + hydrogen gas. Reactivity: Na > K > Ca > Mg > Fe.

QuestionText: Mineral is defined as:
Options: A) Any substance with metal content
B) Naturally occurring substance containing a metal compound
Explanation: Mineral: naturally occurring compound of metal in Earth's crust. Ore: mineral from which metal can be profitably extracted. Not all minerals are ores.

QuestionText: Metals like Na, Ca, Mg react with cold water vigorously. Fe reacts with:
Options: D) No water at any temperature
Explanation: Iron reacts with steam: 3Fe + 4H₂O (steam) → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂. Iron doesn't react with cold or hot liquid water. Very reactive metals (Na, K) react with cold water.

QuestionText: Brass is an alloy of:
Explanation: Brass = Cu + Zn (70:30 typically). Bronze = Cu + Sn. Steel = Fe + C. Duralumin = Al + Cu + Mn + Mg.

QuestionText: Anodising aluminium:
Options: B) Adds thick oxide layer for protection and decoration
D) Electroplates it with another metal
Explanation: Anodising: electrochemical process that thickens the natural Al₂O₃ layer. More corrosion resistant, can be dyed. Used in aircraft, phone casings.

QuestionText: The extraction of metals from ores involves:
Options: B) Reduction of metal compounds (removal of oxygen/non-metal)
Explanation: Extraction = reduction (metal compound → metal). Methods: carbon reduction (Fe, Cu), electrolytic reduction (Al, Na), thermite reaction, hydrometallurgy.

QuestionText: Aqua regia dissolves gold because it is:
Options: A) A mixture of HCl and H₂SO₄
B) A mixture of 3:1 conc. HCl and conc. HNO₃ (extremely corrosive)
D) A mixture of acids and bases
Explanation: Aqua regia = 3 parts conc. HCl : 1 part conc. HNO₃. Only mixture that dissolves noble metals (Au, Pt). HNO₃ oxidises, Cl⁻ from HCl forms stable complexes (AuCl₄⁻).

QuestionText: The hardest naturally occurring substance is:
Explanation: Diamond: hardest natural substance (10 on Mohs scale). Each carbon forms 4 strong covalent bonds in 3D tetrahedral network. Used for cutting tools.

QuestionText: Electroplating uses:
Options: B) Electrolysis to deposit a thin layer of metal
Explanation: Electroplating: object (cathode) placed in solution of metal ions + current → metal deposits on object. Used for protection (chrome plating), decoration (gold plating).

QuestionText: Solder is an alloy of:
Explanation: Solder = Pb + Sn (lead-tin alloy). Low melting point → used to join electronic components (though lead-free solders now common: Sn-Ag-Cu).

QuestionText: Non-metals generally have:
Options: C) Poor conductivity and low density
Explanation: Non-metals: poor conductors (except graphite), low density, low melting points (except diamond, carbon), dull (not lustrous), brittle as solids.

QuestionText: The element that is a non-metal but conducts electricity is:
Explanation: Graphite (allotrope of carbon) is the only non-metal that conducts electricity — due to delocalised electrons. Used in dry cell batteries, electrodes, pencil 'lead'.

QuestionText: Rusting is prevented by:
Explanation: Rusting prevention: barrier methods (painting, oiling, greasing), galvanisation, electroplating, making alloys (stainless steel), using more noble metals.

QuestionText: Ionic bonds form between:
Options: B) A metal and a non-metal (transfer of electrons)
Explanation: Ionic bond: metal (low ionisation energy) transfers electron(s) to non-metal (high electron affinity). Metal → cation (+). Non-metal → anion (-). Electrostatic attraction.

QuestionText: Covalent bonds form between:
Explanation: Covalent bond: formed by sharing electrons between atoms. Usually between non-metals. H₂, O₂, H₂O, CO₂, CH₄ are all covalent compounds.

QuestionText: The process by which ores are concentrated before extraction is called:
Explanation: Beneficiation/ore dressing: removes gangue (impurities) from ore to concentrate metal content. Methods: gravity separation, froth flotation, magnetic separation.

QuestionText: An amalgam is an alloy of:
Explanation: Amalgam: alloy containing mercury. Dental amalgam (Ag-Hg). Na amalgam used in NaOH production. Gold amalgamation used in gold mining.

QuestionText: Calamine (ZnCO₃) is an ore of:
Explanation: Zinc ores: calamine (ZnCO₃), zinc blende (ZnS), zincite (ZnO). Copper ores: cuprite (Cu₂O), chalcopyrite (CuFeS₂).

QuestionText: Metal oxides react with acids to form:
Explanation: Metal oxide (basic oxide) + acid → salt + water. CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O. This is a neutralisation-type reaction.

QuestionText: The most reactive metal is:
Explanation: Potassium (K) is at the top of the reactivity series — most reactive metal. Reacts explosively with water. Order: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag > Au.

QuestionText: Phosphorus, sulphur, and iodine are examples of:
Explanation: P, S, and I₂ are solid non-metals. Non-metals occupy the right side of periodic table (except H). About 22 non-metals vs ~90+ metals.

QuestionText: Silicon is classified as a:
Explanation: Silicon: metalloid/semiconductor. Has intermediate properties between metals and non-metals. Used in computer chips (transistors). Other metalloids: Ge, As, Sb, Te.

QuestionText: Smelting is the process of:
Options: B) Reducing metal oxide with carbon at high temperature
Explanation: Smelting: heating ore with reducing agent (carbon/coke) at high temperature to extract metal. Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ (blast furnace).

QuestionText: Tin cans are made of steel coated with:
Explanation: Food cans: steel coated with tin (tinplate). Tin resists corrosion and is non-toxic. If coating breaks, steel underneath corrodes faster because tin is below Fe in reactivity.

QuestionText: The colour of copper sulphate crystals is:
Explanation: Copper sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO₄·5H₂O) = blue crystals. Anhydrous CuSO₄ = white powder. Used to test for water (white → blue when water present).

QuestionText: Gold is alloyed with copper or silver because:
Options: B) Pure gold is too soft for jewellery — alloying increases hardness
Explanation: Pure gold (24 carat) is too soft for jewellery. Mixed with Cu or Ag → 22 carat, 18 carat gold (harder, more durable). Carat indicates gold purity.

QuestionText: Hydrogen is sometimes placed with metals in the reactivity series. In reactions, it:
Options: A) Always acts as a metal
B) Reacts with bases to form salts
C) Is displaced by metals above it in the series
D) Is more reactive than all metals
Explanation: H is in the reactivity series between Pb and Cu. Metals above H (Mg, Zn, Fe) displace H₂ from acids. Cu, Ag, Au (below H) cannot displace H₂ from acids.
